subject: Cooking
title: Sea Salt Isn't Healthier Than Table Salt
description: A fast breakdown of Sea Salt Isn't Healthier Than Table Salt for builders.

hook.text: Gourmet sea salt costs 20x more than table salt. Health-wise, they're virtually identical.

buildup.text: Both sea salt and table salt are 97–99% sodium chloride. The remaining 1–3% is trace minerals.

discovery.text: Sea salt's trace minerals are in amounts too small to have any nutritional impact — milligrams per serving.

twist.text: Table salt is actually fortified with iodine — a nutrient that prevents thyroid disease in 2 billion at-risk people.

climax.text: Sea salt's real advantage is texture and flavor variety (flake, coarse, smoked) — not health.

punchline.text: Sea salt is a better garnish. Table salt is better medicine.

quiz.question: What health advantage does table salt have over sea salt?
options: Iodine fortification that prevents thyroid disease

details.summary: Sea salt and table salt contain the same active ingredient: sodium chloride. Trace minerals in sea salt exist in negligible amounts that provide no health benefit. The main differences are texture and taste, not nutritional value. Both should be consumed in moderation.
details.whyItMatters: Sea salt's premium price and health halo lead people to believe they are making a healthier choice. In terms of sodium content and health impact, all salts are nutritionally equivalent.
takeaways: Both are 97 to 99 percent sodium chloride by composition
Trace minerals in sea salt are too small to affect health
Table salt contains added iodine, which prevents thyroid disorders

faq.question: Does sea salt have less sodium than table salt?
faq.answer: By weight, sea salt and table salt contain nearly identical sodium. Coarse sea salt may have slightly less sodium per teaspoon because the crystals pack less densely, but gram for gram they are equivalent. Switching to sea salt does not reduce sodium intake.

faq.question: Is iodized table salt better for health?
faq.answer: In one important way, yes. Iodine deficiency causes thyroid disorders and was widespread before iodized salt was introduced. If your diet includes little seafood or dairy, iodized salt provides an essential micronutrient that sea salt and Himalayan salt lack.
